name: Clenshaw–Curtis quadrature
definition: On [−1,1], interpolate f at x_j=cos(jπ/n), j=0,…,n; write p_n(x)=Σ_k a_k T_k(x) and approximate integral by Σ_(even k) 2a_k/(1−k²).
variables: n polynomial degree; T_k Chebyshev polynomial; a_k interpolant coefficients
assumptions: Finite evaluations on a closed interval; well-defined integrable function
limitations: Nonsmooth integrands can converge slowly; endpoint singularities require separate treatment
failure_conditions: Nonfinite samples or unresolved quadrature error

name: Adaptive Gauss–Kronrod quadrature
definition: For each interval I compute nested Gauss and Kronrod estimates G(I), K(I), with local indicator E(I)=|K(I)−G(I)|; subdivide intervals with largest E until summed indicators meet declared tolerance or budget.
variables: I subinterval; G,K nested quadrature estimates; E local indicator
assumptions: Integrable function and valid nested nodes and weights on the reference interval
limitations: Difference indicator is not a guaranteed upper error bound; singular or oscillatory integrands can defeat sampling
failure_conditions: Nonfinite evaluations, unresolved error, or exhausted subdivisions
computation: Provisional adaptive interval management with nested rules; review exact node/weight and stopping specification before admission.
